text:
maria: FYI — we started seeing p95/p99 generation latency jump in na-east (NA1) around 08:12 UTC. Baseline ~120ms, now lots of tails in 800ms-1.2s range. Seems coincident with the runtime change rolled at ~08:05 (kv cache TTL tuning + batching tweak).

arjun: can you paste the dashboard? logs?

maria: https://grafana.redwood/NaEast/latency -> batcher queue length up x5, gpu utilization spiky, kvcache hit-rate dropped ~20%. Logs show repeated cache misses + memfree churn. Also seeing increased pre-emptions on some pods.

sophie: tagging @infra-oncall — sounds like cache parameter change is causing churn and larger effective seqlen for the runtime, which inflates batch sizes and kills latency. Recommend diverting traffic off NA1 while we diagnose.

infra-oncall: doing diversion now — shifting 30% traffic to NA2 and 20% to NA-west. Scaling hotpool +8 GPUs as a buffer.

kai: any chance this is a model change rather than infra? which commit rolled?

maria: deploy-bot shows rollout id deploy-2026-04-21-08:05 by runtime-team, change: kvcache.ttl from 5m -> 10s, batcher.window_ms 60 -> 120. The short TTL would explain cache misses.

arjun: ouch. TTL 10s explains eviction churn. That + larger batching window causes big, infrequent batches that increase tail latency. We should revert TTL first and reduce batcher.window_ms temporarily.

sophie: agree — prefer config hotfix instead of full rollback if possible. We can flip runtime flags via runtime-config service.

infra-oncall: applying config rollback for kvcache.ttl -> 5m in NA1 now, and overriding batcher.window_ms=60 globally for production. Command used: 
```
$ rctl runtime-config set --env prod --region na1 --key kvcache.ttl --value 300
$ rctl runtime-config set --env prod --region na1 --key batcher.window_ms --value 60
```

deploy-bot: runtime-config change accepted (txn 0x8b3f), propagation to workers started.

maria: metrics starting to improve — kvcache hit-rate back up ~18% within 90s, batcher queue length falling. p95 now ~200-220ms. Still watching for stragglers.

kai: good catch. We should gate future TTL/batcher changes with a canary on <5% traffic for 30m and add an automated rollback if kvcache hit-rate drops >10%.

arjun: +1. Also add a short-term mitigation: enable prefix-caching for hot prefixes to avoid full eviction recurrence. Config: 
```
$ rctl runtime-config set --env prod --region na1 --key kvcache.prefix_only --value true
```

infra-oncall: added the prefix-caching toggle to NA1 canary group. Diverted remaining 10% through NA2 until metrics stable.

sophie: schedule follow-up postmortem and add test in staging that simulates short TTLs with real seqlen distribution. We keep frank rollback plan documented.

maria: summary: 08:05 rollout changed kvcache.ttl->10s and batcher.window_ms->120, caused cache thrash + oversized batches => latency tails. Emergency mitigation: reverted ttl to 5m and restored batcher.window_ms=60, enabled prefix caching, shifted traffic to NA2/NA-west, scaled hotpool +8 GPUs. Latency recovering. Next: canary gating, alert rule on kvcache hit-rate drop, staging test, and postmortem doc.

kai: putting an action item for runtime-team: "rework TTL change plan + canary + automated rollback". I'll create the incident ticket.

maria: thanks everyone. keeping thread open for one hour to confirm stability. :thumbsup:
